question.text: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>T</mi></math> be the line passing through the points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> and <math><mi>Q</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfenced></math>. Let <math><msub><mrow><mi>F</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> be the set of all pairs of circles <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>S</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mi>S</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>T</mi></math> is tangents to <math><msub><mrow><mi>S</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> and tangent to <math><msub><mrow><mi>S</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math>, and also such that <math><msub><mrow><mi>S</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi>S</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> touch each other at a point, say, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>M</mi></math>. Let <math><msub><mrow><mi>E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> be the set representing the locus of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>M</mi></math> as the pair <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>S</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi> </mi><msub><mrow><mi>S</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced></math> varies in <math><msub><mrow><mi>F</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math>. Let the set of all straight line segments joining a pair of distinct points of <math><msub><mrow><mi>E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and passing through the point <math><mi>R</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>1,1</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> be <math><msub><mrow><mi>F</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> . Let <math><msub><mrow><mi>E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> be the set of the mid-points of the line segments in the set <math><msub><mrow><mi>F</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> . Then, which of the following statement(s) is (are) TRUE?

options.text: The point <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mfenced></math> does NOT lie in <math><msub><mrow><mi>E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math>

The point <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mfenced></math> does NOT lie in <math><msub><mrow><mi>E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math>

solution.text:
AP=AQ=AM So ∠PMQ=90°
Locus of M is a circle having PQ as its diameter
Hence, E1: x2+y2-2y-39=0, x≠±2
Clearly -2,7 is not included in the locus because we can not consider point circles, and 0,32 does not lie on E1 as it does not satisfy the equation above.

The equation of chord with Bh,k as mid point will be given by T=S1 or

xh+yk-y-k-39=h2+k2-2k-39

or xh+yk-y+k=h2+k2

It passes through R1,1. So,

h+k-1+k=h2+k2

or the locus of E2 is x2+y2-x-2y+1=0

But if P is not the part of locus of M then PQ is not the chord of locus of M. So point 45,75 does not lie in E2. 12,1 does not satisfy the equation hence does not lie in E2.
